verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Equivalent after one trivial rewriting at the left endpoint. The force class matches exactly: ContDiff ℝ ∞ f together with HasCompactSupport f and tsupport f ⊆ Ioi 0 ×ˢ univ is the zero extension of an element of C_c^∞(ℝ³ × (0,∞); ℝ³), which the file's own docstring says it is intended to encode; compactness is in space-time, as the paper's notation requires (the Lean construction even puts the support in K × [0,2] via compactForce and PositiveTimeForce.force). The residual ℛ is navierStokesResidual at ν = 1, matching (3.1) term for term. The only apparent gap is the left endpoint: the paper asserts ℛ(u,p) = f for 0 ≤ t < 1, whereas CandidateProperties.navier_stokes asserts it for t ∈ Ioo 0 1, and all residual clauses found in the repository use Ioo (ProblemStatement.lean:112, MaximalLifespan.lean:35, R3CompactCandidate.lean:36, R3/ProblemStatement.lean:106); the stated reason is that ordinary derivatives at positive times avoid differentiating an arbitrary extension past t = 0. The closed endpoint is nevertheless stated in Lean: ParabolicScaling.zeroBefore_residual (R3/ParabolicCalculus.lean:71) concludes navierStokesResidual ν (zeroBefore u) (zeroBefore p) t x = f (t, x) for every t < 1 — hence at t = 0 and below — from CandidateProperties together with the hypothesis that u and p vanish for |t| ≤ 3/8, and that hypothesis is supplied for the actual candidate by ActualCandidate.selected_candidate_one_with_initial_rest (R3/ActualCandidate.lean:143). The rewriting back to the candidate's own fields is trivial: zeroBefore g z = g z for z.1 ≥ 0 (zeroBefore_eq_of_nonneg, R3/DelayedExtension.lean:23), and near t = 0 the two pairs agree outright — u, p vanish on |t| ≤ 3/8 and zeroBefore u, zeroBefore p vanish on t ≤ 3/8 (zeroBefore_eq_zero_of_le, R3/DelayedExtension.lean:42) — so residual_congr (R3/ParabolicCalculus.lean:61) transfers the identity at (0, x) to u, p themselves, with f(0, ·) = 0 on both sides by CompactPositiveTimeSupport.eq_zero_of_nonpos.
